<a id="create-paths-of-travel"></a>

### Create paths of travel

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-14 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** draw a path of travel in a floor plan - Analyze > Route Analysis > Path of Travel - from rooms or points to one named exit door or point, each length read back.

Draws path of travel lines in a floor plan - Revit's Analyze > Route Analysis > Path of Travel - from rooms (by number or name, or every room on the level) or points in millimetres to one exit: a door named by its Mark, or a point. Revit finds each route around the walls. Each new line's length is read back in metres, and any start Revit found no path from is named with Revit's status. The exit is never guessed. Deletes nothing.

**How to use it**

1. Open the model in Revit and connect Heron: press **Heron** on the Heron tab, so its heron turns orange.
2. Turn **Changes** on in Heron's **Settings** (Heron tab).

<a id="create-room-separation-lines"></a>

### Create room separation lines

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-02 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** draw a room separation line across this opening.

Draws room separation lines - or space separation lines, when asked - along a run of points in one plan view. The line Revit's own Room Separator draws: it bounds a room where there is no wall, so a kitchen and a living room joined by an open archway become two rooms instead of one. **NOTHING COULD DRAW ONE BEFORE THIS.** Found 2026-10-02 drawing a shop-and-flat plan in Project2 (Revit 2024): the kitchen and the living room were joined by a 900 mm opening, PLACE_ROOM_AT_POINT made one room of both because nothing bounded the gap, and no fragment called the API that makes a separation line (FRAGMENT-ISSUES row 5b-289). A plain line from DRAW_FAMILY_DETAIL_LINES does not bound a room - it is a drawing or reference line, a different category Revit's room boundary never reads. **ROOM OR SPACE IS THE CALLER'S WORD, AND IT MUST BE SAID.** A room separation line bounds rooms and a space separation line bounds MEP spaces, and neither bounds the other: a kitchen split for the architect is still one space for the heating load. `lineKind` space draws the space kind. The two look alike on a plan, so every line made is read back and its category reported. **A RUN OF POINTS, like CREATE_WALL.** Consecutive points make the lines: two points is one line across an opening, and a run whose last point repeats the first is a closed loop. Points are millimetres when typed; Heron converts them to internal feet at the boundary (D-67), so no length is converted a second time. **THE LINES LIE ON THE VIEW'S OWN LEVEL.** Only the plan position of each point is used. The height is the plane of the level the plan belongs to, read off the sketch plane Revit makes on that level rather than worked out by hand - where levels are measured to a survey datum, a level's two heights differ (ProjectElevation is the one the API draws at), and the wrong one puts the lines where no room is. **REFUSED, WITH THE REASON, RATHER THAN THROWN:** a family document (a family has no rooms to bound), a view template, a view with no level of its own (a section, a 3D view, a sheet), and fewer than two points. A pair closer together than Revit's own shortest line is counted in `tooShort` and the rest of the run is still drawn; a pair Revit itself refuses is named in `refused` and the rest still drawn. **READ BACK, NOT ASSUMED.** Every line is fetched again by its id after it is made, and what is reported is what came back: how many, which category Revit filed each one under, their ends in millimetres and their total length. **IT PLACES NO ROOM AND JOINS NOTHING.** Splitting a room that already exists is two steps: this line, then PLACE_ROOMS at a point for the half that has no room. What Revit does to the existing room when the line cuts it, and the warning it gives for a line lying on a wall or on another separation line, are Revit's, and are recorded by the proof rather than claimed. **VERSION 2 DRAWS AREA BOUNDARY LINES TOO** - lineKind area, in the area plan named, along a run of points, round the exterior walls at a face, or along closed loops. The kind - room, space or area - is always said. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="place-rooms"></a>

### Place rooms

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-02 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** fill every enclosed area on this level with rooms, or with spaces.

Places a room - or an MEP space - in every enclosed area on one level, in one pass. **Spaces are the MEP half and they are not rooms.** An architectural model carries Rooms; an MEP model needs Spaces, and heating and cooling loads, airflow and every space-based schedule depend on them existing and being bounded. The two are indistinguishable to look at and are different elements, so which one is wanted is asked for, never guessed. **A space can be placed where a room already is**, and normally is - the room belongs to the architect's model, the space to yours, and they occupy the same air. So finding rooms already there is not a reason to refuse. **Anything not enclosed gets nothing**, and that list is the useful half of the answer - see the note below the contract for what it actually tells you. Version 2 places them at chosen points as well - `points` - with the phase and the kind asked for there too. Version 3 places areas too - placeKind area, in the area plan named, at the points given, with names and numbers in point order.

### Report area volume computations

**DRAFT - runs in a chat, and its answer says so.** It changes nothing in the model, so it is not refused, but it has not been proved on a real model yet.

**What it does:** the Area and Volume Computations settings - volumes on or off, where room areas are measured, and every area scheme.

Answers whether this project computes volumes - Revit's volume calculation for rooms and spaces - where its room areas are measured, the room boundary taken at the wall finish, the wall center, the core layer or the core center, and which area schemes it has, read from Revit's Area and Volume Computations dialog (Architecture > Room & Area), both tabs, in the words the dialog shows. COMPUTATIONS: Volume Computations - Areas only or Areas and Volumes - and Room Area Computation - At wall finish, At wall center, At wall core layer or At wall core center. AREA SCHEMES: every scheme, with its description, whether it is the Gross Building one, and how many areas and area plans it holds. It changes nothing and asks for nothing. **"IS VOLUME COMPUTATION ON?" IS ANSWERED HERE (D-86).** A question about these settings needs nothing changed, so it is read, never written. Built on 2026-10-06 after a lookup found no tool: the model "Heron loads test" had no Space volumes while Revit computed areas only (FRAGMENT-ISSUES row 5b-327). **A VOLUME OF ZERO IS USUALLY THIS SETTING, NOT THE ROOM.** With Areas only, Revit computes no volume and a schedule reads as a building with none. So beside the setting the answer counts the placed, bounded rooms and spaces and how many of them have a volume right now - the switch and what it does to this model, read together. **SPACES ARE ASKED ABOUT, NOT ASSUMED.** The dialog shows one Room Area Computation; Revit's API takes the kind of spatial element as an argument. What Revit answers for Spaces is reported as Revit's answer, and said plainly if it differs from rooms. **AN AREA SCHEME WITH NO AREAS IS STILL LISTED.** REPORT_AREAS reaches a scheme only through the Areas placed in it, so a scheme nobody has used yet is invisible there. The counts beside each scheme are what deleting it in the dialog would take with it - its area plans and their areas - which is why Heron offers no delete (Constitution Article 7). In a family document it says the settings belong to a project, and reports nothing else.

<a id="report-room-space-data"></a>

### Report room space data

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-02 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** the room and space schedule - number, name, level, area and volume.

The room and space table: number, name, level, area and volume for every Room or MEP Space given. Read-only, and it works on both categories at once because they share one base type - number, name, level and area are the same properties on each. **A ZERO VOLUME IS USUALLY A SETTING, NOT A ROOM.** Room volumes are only computed when *Area and Volume Computations* is set to compute volumes; with it off - which is the Revit default - EVERY room reports zero. Reporting those zeros as numbers produces a schedule that says the building has no volume, and somebody then goes looking for the modelling fault. Ids with no computed volume are named in `volumeNotComputed` instead, so the answer says which switch to turn on rather than handing over a column of noughts. Spaces compute volume without that switch, so a mixed set can legitimately have the volume for its spaces and not for its rooms. **AN UNPLACED ROOM IS NOT AN UNENCLOSED ONE, AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS A MODELLING FAULT.** Both report zero area. A room with no location was never put in the model - it sits in the schedule waiting to be placed. A room with a location and no area was placed somewhere its boundaries do not close. They are told apart here by asking for the location, and named separately, because the first is deleted or placed and the second is a wall or a room-bounding setting to fix. **OCCUPANCY AND THE OTHER TEXT COLUMNS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT HERE.** Reading one named parameter off a set of elements is `READ_ELEMENT_PARAMETERS`, which already handles the instance-then-type lookup and says which elements simply do not carry it. Adding a column here would be a second place that reads parameters, and the two would drift. Version 2 also gives each one's length and width along its own walls, its rotation, and how far from rectangular it is. Areas are square feet, volumes cubic feet and lengths feet - Revit's internal units, per D-20, converted at the edge where the user is. ASSUMES NOTHING ABOUT TRANSACTIONS - it opens none and needs none.

| **Works on** | what is selected in Revit: elements |
| **You get** | identities, areas, volumes, unplaced, unenclosed, volume not computed, lengths, widths, rotations, irregular, volume computation off |
| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |
| **Proved on Revit** | 2020 |
| **Capability** | `REPORT_ROOM_SPACE_DATA` |

<a id="set-area-volume-computations"></a>

### Set area volume computations

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-10-18 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** set Area and Volume Computations - switch between Areas only and Areas and Volumes, change where room areas are measured, make or rename area schemes.

Switches Revit's Volume Computations between Areas only and Areas and Volumes, changes where every room's area is measured, and makes, renames or re-describes area schemes - a new one, a new name for one, Rentable say, or a new description - in Area and Volume Computations (Architecture > Room & Area), both tabs, set in the words the dialog shows. COMPUTATIONS: Volume Computations to Areas only or Areas and Volumes; Room Area Computation to At wall finish, At wall center, At wall core layer or At wall core center. AREA SCHEMES: a new scheme, a new name for one, or a new description. Built on 2026-10-06: the model "Heron loads test" needed Areas and Volumes before its Spaces had volumes, nothing in Heron could change it, and the modeller did it by hand (FRAGMENT-ISSUES row 5b-327). **ADMIN, BEHIND THE OWNER'S ADMIN SWITCH (D-106).** These are how the project is set up, not an edit to an element. Room Area Computation re-measures EVERY room in the project at once - every room schedule, tag and anything reading a room's Area moves with it - and an area scheme is a classification the whole team works inside, the reason CREATE_WORKSET is ADMIN. One card carries one risk, so the whole dialog is ADMIN, renaming included. A chat should say what a Room Area Computation change does to every room before asking for it. **NO DELETE.** Deleting an area scheme deletes its area plans and the areas on them (Constitution Article 7), so it stays in the dialog, where Revit says what goes with it. **A NEW SCHEME IS A COPY OF AN ORDINARY ONE.** Revit's API has no call that makes an area scheme from nothing, on any release 2020 to 2027. The dialog's New makes an ordinary, non-Gross Building scheme, so one is copied with ElementTransformUtils.CopyElement, renamed, given the description asked for (or none), and checked: it must not be a Gross Building scheme, and no area plan or area may come with it. A project holding only the Gross Building scheme is refused by name - make the first ordinary scheme with the dialog's New. **EVERYTHING IS CHECKED FIRST, AND READ BACK AFTER.** A word the dialog does not show, a scheme that is not there, a name Revit refuses or one already taken stops the call with nothing changed. A setting already as asked is counted and left alone. After the last write every setting and scheme is read again; one that does not read as asked fails the call and the host rolls the whole call back. When Volume Computations changes, the placed rooms and spaces with a volume are counted before and after, so the answer shows what the switch did to this model. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="set-room-limits"></a>

### Set room limits

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-10-18 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** set where these rooms or spaces stop at the top - a level and an offset.

Sets the top of each room or MEP space handed in - its Upper Limit, a level, and its Limit Offset from that level - together, in one undo. **NOTHING ELSE COULD TIE A ROOM'S TOP TO A LEVEL.** WRITE_ELEMENT_PARAMETERS refuses a parameter that stores an element id, deliberately, because "Level 2" as text is a name and not a level. So a room's height could be changed by its offset but never measured from the level above. Here the level arrives resolved by name - refused if two levels share it - and is written as that level. **BOTH ARE SET TOGETHER, BECAUSE EITHER ALONE MOVES THE TOP.** Change the level and keep the offset and the top jumps by the distance between the levels. On 2026-09-24, in Project1, one room's Upper Limit was moved to Level 2 by hand with its offset left at +3700, and its top went 3700 mm above Level 2, through the slab. The caller names the level and the offset, and the top they make is worked out before anything is written. **A TOP AT OR BELOW THE ROOM'S OWN FLOOR IS REFUSED**, per room, before anything is written to it - the floor being the room's level plus its base offset. **ROOMS AND SPACES ALIKE**, told apart by category, since both carry the same Upper Limit and Limit Offset. Anything else - an Area included - is named and left alone. **EVERY ONE IS READ BACK** after one regeneration: the level it names and the offset it holds. One whose values did not stick is named, never counted. It does not decide how high a room should go - that is the caller's. The house rule recorded 2026-09-24 is rooms to the underside of the slab above and MEP spaces to the ceiling; the VA BIM Manual v2.2 (2023), 2.13.1, puts both to the underside of the deck with ceilings as bounding elements. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

| **You get** | changed, findings |
| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |
| **Proved on Revit** | 2020 |
| **Capability** | `SET_ROOM_LIMITS` |
